title: Exceptions and debugging
runtime: Modern evergreen browser or Node.js with ES modules. Run fragments in browser DevTools or a small .js file unless the example says otherwise.

diagnostic.question: Can you explain the main purpose of exceptions and debugging before reading?
diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: An exception changes control flow
sections.body: throw immediately stops normal execution and searches outward for a matching catch. Throw Error objects rather than plain strings so the message and stack are useful. Use exceptions for failures a caller may handle, not as a replacement for every normal branch.

sections.title: Handle or rethrow
sections.body: A catch block receives the thrown value. It can recover with a fallback, add context and rethrow, or report the failure to the user or logs. An empty catch hides evidence and can leave the program in a false success state. finally runs for cleanup even when control returns or throws.

sections.title: A repeatable debugging loop
sections.body: First reproduce the smallest failing case and state expected versus actual behavior. Read the earliest relevant error and stack, inspect the inputs, then form one hypothesis. Use a breakpoint, watch value, or focused log to test it; make the smallest correction and rerun the original and nearby cases.

sections.title: Design for debuggability
sections.body: Small functions, clear names, explicit boundaries, and stable data shapes reduce the search area. Validate external input early and include useful context in errors without exposing secrets. Tests preserve known behavior, while source maps and browser DevTools connect runtime evidence to the original code.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Exceptions and debugging is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain exceptions and debugging to a junior developer.
interviewQuestions.answer: Explain what throwing changes. Catch at the boundary that can act. Use evidence before editing code. Make failures easier to find.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Show a small example and one common mistake.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using exceptions and debugging behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which edge case would you test first?

interviewQuestions.question: Where can exceptions and debugging affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.

mastery.policy: Reading or opening a solution is guided exposure, not mastery. Save an attempt, solve again without help, explain the rule, and transfer it to a new problem.

commonMistakes.symptom: Code using exceptions and debugging produces a surprising value.
commonMistakes.cause: The result was run before the value, type, scope, identity, or control flow was predicted.
commonMistakes.fix: Reduce the case, write the expected result, and apply the exact rule from the matching section.

commonMistakes.symptom: A learner copies syntax but cannot adapt it.
commonMistakes.cause: The example was memorized without explaining why it works.
commonMistakes.fix: Change the data and names, predict again, and explain which behavior must stay the same.

commonMistakes.symptom: A React problem is blamed on React immediately.
commonMistakes.cause: The underlying JavaScript behavior was not isolated first.
commonMistakes.fix: Reproduce the value or function behavior in a small JavaScript example, then reconnect it to the component.
